solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bruiser with power breaking additional window

indicators.note: the power letter breaks into the bruiser word, splitting it open

parts.note: a pounder is one who pounds, a bruiser
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A thug with clout smashes an extra window, a picture of break-in violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' puts P inside POUNDER. 'Window' looks like glass, but the answer is a computer window that opens behind the one you are viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-under is an advertising browser window that opens beneath the main page, an extra one the user did not ask for.

clue.text: Part of mum's hose giving dad a whack?

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
a sock is a hard blow, a whack

explanation.surface: Mum's stocking becomes a weapon for hitting dad, a little domestic farce.
explanation.walkthrough: A popsock is a knee-length nylon stocking, hence only part of what full-length hose would cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Popsocks are short nylon stockings, a kind of women's hosiery reaching only to the knee.

clue.text: King Cole in a bad way? Soon one's out at the elbows

indicators.note: something in a bad way is in disorder, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex
anon is an old word meaning soon

explanation.surface: Old King Cole, down on his luck, will soon be shabby, out at the elbows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bad way' rearranges COLE into OLEC. 'Out at the elbows' is an idiom for ragged clothes, but here it is literal: the bone that sticks out at the elbow.
explanation.definitionFit: The olecranon is the bony projection of the ulna that forms the point of the elbow.

clue.text: Indian tree, one replacing millions of others?

indicators.note: one letter is put in the place of another within a word, as replacing says

parts.note: palms are other trees, so the tree context makes others stand for them
M is the abbreviation for million(s)
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: An Indian tree is described as standing in for millions of others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Others' only works because the definition sets up trees: other trees, here palms. 'Replacing' puts A in the place of the M of PALMS.
explanation.definitionFit: The palas is the dhak or flame-of-the-forest, a flowering tree of India.

clue.text: It helps steersman, one in bed, laid up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, upwards
the one letter goes in the bed word

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed
A means one

explanation.surface: A helmsman who is ill in bed, laid up, can hardly steer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid up' reads as ill in bed, but it reverses DIAVAN (A in DIVAN) in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A navaid is any navigational aid, such as a radio beacon, that helps a pilot or helmsman find the way.

clue.text: Labiate late, tended poorly

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A plant has been looked after late and badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' rearranges LATE TENDED. Labiate is a botanical term for plants of the mint family, which has lipped flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dead-nettle is a plant of the mint family Labiatae, so it is an example of a labiate.

clue.text: Channel for water to flow in runnel

indicators.note: the flow word goes in the runnel word

parts.note: a rill is a small stream, a runnel
to go can mean to flow or run, as a liquid does

explanation.surface: A channel lets water flow into a small stream.
explanation.walkthrough: A rigoll is an old word, still in Chambers, for a ring-shaped channel or groove.
explanation.definitionFit: A rigoll is a groove or runnel, a channel along which water can run.

clue.text: Seed covering ball is there? He belts it possibly

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be rearranged into another form

parts.note: the composite anagram's full fodder
the letters that join the answer to make up the fodder

explanation.surface: A batsman asks where the ball is: he belts it, possibly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' says BALL IS THERE could be rearranged as HE BELTS plus the answer, so take the letters of HE BELTS away and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An aril is the fleshy outer coat round some seeds, such as the red cup of the yew.

clue.text: Cook's jelly I see extracted from fungus

indicators.note: the I and see letters are drawn out of the fungus word

parts.note: agaric is a type of mushroom fungus
I see gives the letters I and C, which sound like I see

explanation.surface: A cook makes jelly from a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: I SEE gives IC: I plus C, the letter named like see. 'Extracted from' takes IC out of AGARIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelling substance from seaweed used in cooking as a vegetarian substitute for gelatine.

clue.text: Food cooked in roast

indicators.note: cooked means altered or doctored, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Food cooked in a roast.
explanation.definitionFit: Rations are fixed allowances of provisions, so the word is a plural synonym for food supplies.

clue.text: Sun rising round East? Many of us enjoy summer birthdays

definitions.text: Many of us enjoy summer birthdays

indicators.note: the reversed sun word goes round the east letter
in a down clue, rising means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: The sun rising in the east, and summer birthdays: a sunny picture.
explanation.definitionFit: People born under the sign of Leo, from late July to late August, have their birthdays in high summer.

clue.text: Delayed receiving a present sent back — unusually smooth

indicators.note: the delayed word takes in the other letters

parts.note: late means delayed

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse order

parts.note: to give is to present

explanation.surface: A late present sent back, an unusually smooth piece of returns etiquette.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' is a verb here (give). 'Sent back' turns A GIVE into EVIGA, and LATE 'receiving' it gives the answer. 'Unusually' marks the smoothing sense as rare.
explanation.definitionFit: To laevigate is to polish or make smooth, a rare sense beside the usual one of grinding to a fine powder.

clue.text: Positive German football team making money

parts.note: Elf is German for eleven, a football team

explanation.surface: A confident German football side making money.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelf is a disparaging old word for wealth, especially ill-gotten riches.

clue.text: Vintners to get an early feeling for blend of rouges

parts.words: to get an early feeling for
parts.note: to bode is to have a presentiment of, to sense something in advance

indicators.note: a blend mixes things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wine merchants getting an early feel for a blend of red wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blend of' tells you to rearrange ROUGES into GUEROS; 'rouges' looks like red wines, which suits the vintners, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodeguero is a Spanish wine merchant or cellarman, the keeper of a bodega, so these are vintners.

clue.text: Starts going at this speed one's gift for traffic police

indicators.note: starts are the beginnings of the following words, so take their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of these five words spell out the camera's name

explanation.surface: A driver going at this speed hands traffic police an easy catch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts' asks for the first letters of the next five words. A Gatso is a British speed camera, named after the Dutch maker Gatsonides.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed camera catches speeding motorists automatically, so it hands the police their offenders with no effort.

clue.text: Party at the opera house? It benefits investors

parts.note: La Scala in Milan is the famous opera house
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A party at La Scala seems to be something to help investors.
explanation.walkthrough: Investors here are besiegers (to invest a town is to besiege it), not people with money.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalado is an escalade, the scaling of walls with ladders, which serves an army besieging a fortress.

clue.text: Photo on lake that is showing Walter's bird

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photo
a tarn is a small mountain lake
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A photo of a lake showing a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter is Sir Walter Scott, whose Scots usage Chambers records.
explanation.definitionFit: Pictarnie is Scott's word for the tern, a seabird.

clue.text: Light lubricant: treated solid pine with litre (10, two words)

indicators.note: material that is treated is processed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wood treated with oil, a carpenter's finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Spindle oil is a thin, low-viscosity oil for lubricating fast-turning machine spindles.

clue.text: Wolf maybe died having escaped from fair

indicators.note: the died letter has got out of the fair word, leaving it

parts.note: candid means fair or frank
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A wolf which died after escaping from a fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A canid is any member of the dog family, of which the wolf is an example.

clue.text: Writer I put up in disorderly inn, one of several in alley?

indicators.note: the reversed writer and I go inside the jumbled inn
disorderly means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged
in a down clue, put up means the letters are read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: Someone puts a writer up in a rowdy inn with a bowling alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up' turns PEN I into INEP; 'disorderly' makes INN into NIN, and INEP goes 'in' it. The alley is a skittle alley.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninepin is one of the nine skittles set up at the end of an alley for bowling.

clue.text: Get even with church introducing Latin bit of old sophistry

indicators.note: the even word introduces, takes in, the Latin letter

parts.note: e'en is a poetic contraction of even

explanation.surface: Settling a score with the church by bringing in Latin, an old bit of sophistry.
explanation.walkthrough: E'en is the poetic contraction of even; 'introducing' L into it gives ELEN, then CH follows. 'Get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An elench is an archaic word for a logical refutation, especially a sophistical one.

clue.text: Favouring active involvement

parts.note: a plain definition with no wordplay: this was the competition entry, for which solvers wrote their own clue

explanation.walkthrough: This is not really a cryptic definition. It was Azed's competition word: the puzzle printed only a definition (marked with an asterisk) and invited solvers to send in their own clue for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on approach is one in which a person takes a direct, practical part in the work rather than delegating it.

clue.text: King, black chess piece

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
night is darkness, black

explanation.surface: King and black chess pieces on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: The knight is the chessman shaped as a horse's head, moving in an L shape.

clue.text: Not strictly a Mohican cut for harvest celebration

indicators.note: cut means the end of the word is cut off

parts.note: Hawkeye in The Last of the Mohicans is a white scout, adopted by Mohicans but not one of them

explanation.surface: Someone not quite a Mohican, with a haircut, at a harvest festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mohican' suggests a haircut, but it is Cooper's novel: Hawkeye, the white scout, is not strictly one. 'Cut' drops his last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawkey (or hockey) is a traditional English harvest-home feast.

clue.text: Holiday abroad, shortest one if there's no Brie

indicators.note: the cheese word must be absent from the rest

parts.note: briefest means shortest
A means one
taken as the letters of the word itself

explanation.surface: A short holiday abroad with no Brie, a cheese lover's nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brie' looks like the cheese, but 'if there's no' Brie removes those letters from BRIEFEST A, leaving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Festa is Italian for a festival or holiday, so it is a holiday as celebrated abroad.

clue.text: Fug, with being kept in by cold weather

indicators.note: the with letter is held inside the cold weather word

parts.note: frost is cold weather

explanation.surface: A stuffy room when you are shut in by cold weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Frowst is a stale, stuffy warmth in a room, the same thing as a fug.

clue.text: One involved in nocturnal flirting, being of similar character etc

indicators.note: flirting is flighty movement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: A means one

explanation.surface: Someone engaged in night-time flirting, of a similar character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involved in' only adds A to the letters of NOCTURNAL; 'flirting' then mixes them all, so where the A goes does not matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Connatural means of the same nature, or innate, congenital, so akin in character.

clue.text: Region of SW France suggested by the French?

parts.note: the French word for the has two letters, and naming them with and between them makes the clue's wordplay

explanation.surface: A region of south-west France named by the French.
explanation.walkthrough: French for 'the' is LE, and spelling that out as L AND E gives the answer, which is why it is only 'suggested by' the French.
explanation.definitionFit: A lande is a sandy heath of the kind found in the Landes district of south-west France.

clue.text: Such a face suggests one foolish cracksman, first to last

definitions.text: Such a face suggests one foolish

indicators.note: the first letter moves round to the end

parts.note: a yegg is an American word for a safe-breaker, a cracksman

explanation.surface: A foolish safe-cracker shows it on his face.
explanation.walkthrough: Having egg on your face means looking foolish. 'First to last' moves the Y of YEGG to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An eggy face is one with egg on it, the idiom for being made to look a fool.

clue.text: In hollow, a dip through which river runs

definitions.text: In hollow, a dip through which river runs

indicators.note: the answer is found in the next words, running across them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of hollow, then a, then the start of dip

explanation.surface: A river runs through a dip in the hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a wadi is a valley, a dip, where a river runs in the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry rocky valley or watercourse that floods with a river after rain.

clue.text: It's a tight fit in the dressing room — stars almost late

definitions.text: It's a tight fit in the dressing room

parts.note: Leo is a constellation, a group of stars

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: tardy means late

explanation.surface: Stars arrive late at the dressing room, struggling into tight outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' trims the last letter from TARDY to leave TARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A leotard is a tight one-piece garment worn by dancers and gymnasts.

clue.text: Republicans having a bit of a knees-up in lively dance

parts.note: GOP, the Grand Old Party, is the US Republican Party

indicators.note: a bit of means just the first letter is taken

parts.note: a knees-up is British slang for a lively party; its first letter is used

explanation.surface: Republicans enjoying a knees-up, a lively party dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' takes only the first letter of knees-up, British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: The gopak (hopak) is a lively Ukrainian folk dance with high leaps.

clue.text: Places to stay favoured partners at table?

parts.note: in can mean in favour, fashionable
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Places to stay, favoured by partners at the dining table.
explanation.walkthrough: The table is a bridge table, where North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Inns are hotels or pubs offering lodging for travellers.

clue.text: Help for travellers I upset with dog running wild

indicators.note: running wild means out of control, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller is upset by a dog running wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'running wild' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A guidepost is a signpost at a road junction, showing travellers the way.

clue.text: Sex symbol that is given leading part in India

indicators.note: the that word takes the lead, coming before the India letter

parts.note: yon is an old word for that
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sex symbol given a leading part in an Indian film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is given leading part in' puts YON in front of I. 'Sex symbol' suggests a film star, but this is the Hindu symbol of the female principle.
explanation.definitionFit: The yoni is a Hindu stylised representation of the female genitals, worshipped as a symbol of Shakti.

clue.text: Certainly wood growth having nitrogen applied quite recently

parts.note: yes means certainly
a tree is a growth in a wood
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: A forester notes how a new tree has grown since nitrogen was applied recently.
explanation.definitionFit: Yestreen is a Scots and poetic word for yesterday evening, so a time only just past.
